claim: The image builds and runs under the same restrictions as the Kubernetes pod
how: Docker Desktop: read-only filesystem, all capabilities dropped, non-root, offline. Ready in about 6 seconds and returns exactly the golden token ids.

claim: Prometheus scrapes the server, loads every rule, and Grafana provisions the dashboard
how: Compose stack under a real 2 requests per second run: every dashboard query returned data.
source: The compose stack works end to end.

claim: The alert rules are syntactically valid
how: promtool check rules accepts all of them, and a healthy run fired none.

claim: The observability layer costs nothing measurable
how: Same-session A/B on the same configuration and seed: 0.83 req/s before, 0.90 after.

claim: The manifests work on a live cluster
how: They render with kubectl kustomize and unit tests check their consistency, but probes, autoscaling and the drain sequence have not met a real API server.
source: The Kubernetes manifests have not been applied to a real cluster.

claim: An alert actually fires when it should
how: Expressions parse and evaluate, but thresholds are reasoned from the benchmark, not exercised by bad traffic. The burn-rate alert needs an hour of it.
source: No alert has been seen firing.

how: Each step was run by hand locally. The workflow itself has not run because the repository had no remote.
source: The GitHub Actions workflow has never run

claim: This page is live on Cloudflare
how: Deployed with Cloudflare Pages Git integration; a curl of the live URL returns 200 with the CSP, HSTS and cache headers from public/_headers.

claim: Every commit on main is built, published, deployed to Kubernetes and rolled back on a bad release
how: release.yml ran green on GitHub: image pushed to GHCR, rolled out to a kind cluster, smoke-tested, a build that cannot start was contained with no capacity loss and rolled back.
source: requires that capacity never drops and that the rollback restores the previous build

claim: The engine runs in a long-lived production cluster
how: The rollout runs on an ephemeral cluster inside CI. Nothing serves real traffic and no performance gate is part of the pipeline.
source: there is no long-lived production cluster, so nothing serves real traffic
